title: Microsoft 365 Backup: Full Workload Backup policies for SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange
summary: The briefing passes: its configuration paths, automation, pricing and policy behaviour are supported by Microsoft documentation. It accurately distinguishes the roadmap targets, the tenant notice's rollout windows and Learn's continuing preview designation.

claims.claim: Existing backups of removed or excluded protected units remain available according to retention settings.
claims.quote: Regardless, existing backups for that protection unit will remain for its defined retention period.

claims.claim: Removing a unit from Full Workload Backup adds it to the exclusion list.
claims.quote: When you remove a protection unit from the Full Workload Backup policy, it's added to the policy's exclusion list.

claims.claim: Removing a unit from Full Workload Backup stops new backups for that unit.
claims.quote: This keeps Full Workload Backup from automatically re-protecting it again, and no new backups are taken for it.

claims.claim: Turning off Full Workload Backup removes its policy.
claims.quote: After Full Workload Backup is turned off: - The Full Workload Backup policy is removed.

claims.claim: Turning off the policy moves units protected only by it to Removed items.
claims.quote: Protection units associated only with the Full Workload Backup policy move to the Removed items tab.

claims.claim: After shutdown, new backups stop until affected units join a custom policy or Full Workload Backup is re-enabled.
claims.quote: New backups will not be taken, unless and until the protection unit(s) are added to a custom policy or the Full Workload Backup policy is re-enabled.

claims.claim: Removing protection units from backup policies is listed as a potentially harmful notification event.

claims.claim: The charge is based on the size of content added to backup protection.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Backup charges you based on the size of the following content once it's added to backup protection.

claims.claim: The billable content includes deleted SharePoint and OneDrive content in the second-stage recycle bin.
claims.quote: Deleted content in SharePoint sites' and OneDrive accounts' second-stage recycle bin (also known as site collection recycle bin).

claims.claim: The billable mailbox size includes associated online archives.
claims.quote: Size of the live user or shared mailbox plus their associated online archives if those are being used.

claims.claim: Deleted and versioned items in protected mailboxes count towards the charge.
claims.quote: Deleted and versioned items in the protected mailboxes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The documentation does not explicitly state whether Full Workload Backup exclusion-list edits send email notifications.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice instructs administrators to review the coverage summary and confirm policy creation.
